Canadian, so not personally impacted here. But:

There's something I've missed hearing in these discussions and I'd like to hear from you what you think. In Canada, where we have provinces rather than states, every time an even slightly-left party gets elected, the response from Big Money (resources industries, investment, the rich, etc.) is to shut down or move out and reduce the economy until the left-party goes away. In one election in B.C. back in the 1980's as an example, nine thousand loggers were laid off work a week after the NDP won. Mining followed shortly, can't remember the figures on that. But the flow of disposable income dried up instantly.

Likewise with Bernie's take, which I gather is to tax the high end of the economy more. Fine, I understand and approve the idea. But my experience is that Money (note the capital letter) in a situation like this, will just get up from the table and walk away. Banks are worldwide now, money is almost completely fluid, it can just go elsewhere. And if that should happen, people like Bernie will have nothing to work with.

I lament this; but it's a reality, and I don't hear Bernie, or anyone else on the left, talking about that challenge. How could this be handled? It feels as though the oligarchy is pretty well protected from any moves we regular folks might make to redistribute wealth; and the argument that Money interests are destroying the middle class, who are the market for their productions, doesn't seem to cut any ice at all.

Incidentally, I'm not any kind of expert. Just, you know, thinking....

That's part of what Bernie's actually fighting against. Our government has been making it easier and easier for the corporations to export their labor to other countries, which has been drying up the middle class. California and New York have absurd taxes, yet they are both economically powerful. Industry moving across state lines isn't so much an issue as industry moving overseas.

That's the great thing about tariffs, if you impose them on all goods imported, it makes products that are made overseas and then shipped back over here less profitable. The less profitable they are, the less likely manufacturing jobs are to be moved overseas. The more domestic manufacturing jobs we have, we have higher employment numbers, less people will slip into abject poverty and more people are participating in the circulation of money.

More interestingly the Federal Government relied mostly on tariffs to fund itself for a large deal of it's existence. If we impose higher tariffs the government will increase their income without raising taxes (in effect it's taxing the rich for exporting manufacturing jobs), manufacturing jobs will stop moving overseas (and may even crawl back slowly), and people can start working their way out of poverty.

I don't think Sanders has come out and stated that he is pro-tariffs, but he has constantly voted against reducing and removing tariffs, and I feel that ramping up tariffs is one way we could really help our economy.
